text: PWS is a genetic condition that occurs in approximately 1 out of every 15,000–20,000 births. It is typically caused by a deletion on the paternal chromosome 15q11-q13, which accounts for 70–75% of cases. In 20 to 25% of cases, it is caused by maternal disomy of chromosome 15, and in very rare cases (2%), it is caused by unbalanced translocations or imprinting centre defects ( Whittington and Holland, 2017 ). PWS is associated with various cognitive impairments, including deficits in spatial domain as well as attention ( Foti et al., 2015 ). These children often show sustained attention, working memory, and executive functioning challenges that hinder their academic performance ( Foti et al., 2015 ).
source_label: Attention skills, learning and academic abilities in children and adolescents with genetic disorders: a systematic review
